Analysts are questioning Apple's supply chain leverage and the AI impact on its products.

items.title: Rupee gains 30 paise to touch monthly high
items.summary: The Indian rupee closed at 95.38 on Friday, strengthening significantly. Persistent Reserve Bank of India interventions and lower oil prices aided this currency gain. The local unit traded within a narrow range during the trading session. A weaker dollar index also contributed to the rupee's upward movement. Analysts expect continued support for the rupee at lower levels.

items.title: Bajaj Finserv Q1 net up 18% on NBFC strength
items.summary: Bajaj Finserv announced an eighteen percent profit increase for the June quarter. This growth was primarily fueled by strong consumer finance earnings. Bajaj Finance saw its profit after tax rise by twenty-eight percent. However, profits at general and life insurance units experienced declines. Bajaj Housing Finance reported a twenty-three percent profit increase.

items.title: India to get 11 new flying schools to tackle India's 30000+ pilot shortage
items.summary: Airports Authority of India awarded eleven new flying training slots with an aim to boost domestic pilot training capacity. The expansion will help meet the projected demand for over thirty thousand pilots. New facilities will add hundreds of training aircraft and simulators. This initiative will reduce foreign training dependence and retain expenditure within India.

items.title: IRDAI tightens ownership norms, eases capital infusion
items.summary: IRDAI has tightened oversight on insurer ownership changes and eased capital raising. Investors now need prior approval for shareholding changes exceeding five percent. The regulator also extended approval requirements to promoter group transfers. Dilution from existing shareholders not participating is now a transfer event. These amendments were announced late Friday by the authority.

items.title: Sebi bans Zee's Subhash Chandra, Punit Goenka from markets for a year
items.summary: Sebi has barred Zee founder Subhash Chandra and CEO Punit Goenka from the securities market for one year. This action stems from an unauthorized pledge of company land to secure promoter group loans. The regulator also imposed a significant penalty on Zee Entertainment Enterprises Limited. Shareholders approved a convertible warrant issuance, raising promoters' stake substantially. This development follows a previous investor rejection of a similar proposal.

items.title: ITC Q1 profit plunges 27% due to record cigarette taxes and West Asia crisis
items.summary: ITC's first quarter net profit declined twenty-seven percent year-on-year. Record taxation on cigarettes significantly impacted the company's core business operations. The West Asia crisis also negatively affected agri-business exports during the period. However, the FMCG segment showed resilience with revenue and profit growth. Consumption remained steady across rural and urban markets despite inflation concerns.

items.title: Maruti Suzuki Q1 profit drops 11% to Rs 3,352 crore amid rising input costs
items.summary: Maruti Suzuki reported an eleven percent profit decline in the June quarter. Rising input costs, aggravated by West Asia hostilities, impacted profitability significantly. However, net sales climbed thirty-six percent to ₹49,959 crore during the same period. Unit sales also saw a strong twenty-nine percent increase, reaching a record 682,724 cars. The company also approved four compressed bio gas projects with a budget of ₹561 crore.

items.title: Bloomberg delays India’s entry to global bond index yet again
items.summary: The inclusion of Indian government bonds in Bloomberg's Global Aggregate Index has been deferred yet again, as the company requires additional evaluation of both operational and market infrastructure components. This setback could lead to an immediate uptick in sovereign bond yields, surprising investors who were hopeful for increased foreign capital inflow. Meanwhile, Indian bonds remain part of various other emerging market debt indexes.

items.title: IDBI's unlisted share sales not a public issue: Sebi
items.summary: Sebi has clarified that IDBI Bank can sell unlisted shares privately. These transactions will not be considered public issues by the regulator. This clarification allows for privately negotiated deals with identified buyers. IDBI Bank sought this guidance for its holdings in unlisted companies. The move facilitates secondary transfers of equity shares under specific conditions.

items.title: Strong earnings, FPI inflows keep Indian equities resilient despite global risks
items.summary: Indian equity indices wrapped up July on a high note, achieving their best monthly performance in three months with significant gains. The robust corporate earnings played a critical role in alleviating fears related to rising oil prices. The Nifty and Sensex jumped over 2.5% in the week and nearly 2.1% throughout July.

items.title: Sebi disposes of case against Religare Enterprises, Saluja, other persons
items.summary: Sebi has concluded legal actions against Religare Enterprises and its former chairperson. The regulator found no further directions were needed after the open offer. Proceedings were initiated alleging Religare failed to cooperate with the mandatory open offer. The company had questioned the Burman Group's 'fit and proper' status and delayed approvals. The open offer's completion achieved the remedial objective of Sebi's proceedings.

Their average deposit rate remained higher than private sector offerings.

items.title: Unfazed by West Asia crisis, fiscal deficit within range at 18.2% in Q1
items.summary: The Centre's fiscal deficit reached 18.2% of the full-year target in the first quarter. Higher spending was offset by stronger net tax collections, analysts noted. Revenue expenditure rose over 7% year-on-year, driven by increased April spending. Capital expenditure remained strong, increasing 24% year-on-year during the quarter. This data suggests the government will likely meet its fiscal deficit target.

items.title: Floating solar projects to be fired up by Rs 5,000 cr scheme
items.summary: The Cabinet has approved the Pradhan Mantri Surya Sarovar Yojana with a significant outlay. This scheme aims to develop 5,000 MW of floating solar projects with energy storage. Projects will be sanctioned from FY27 to FY31, with financial support extending to FY33. It will utilize existing water bodies, eliminating land competition and strengthening grid reliability. Central aid of ₹1 crore per MW will be provided for eligible projects after commissioning.

items.title: PM-KISAN scheme gets 5-year extension and Rs 3.1 lakh crore
items.summary: The Union Cabinet approved a five-year extension for the PM-KISAN scheme. This extension will continue direct cash transfers to eligible farmer families through FY31. The government committed ₹3.15 lakh crore for this significant initiative. This financial support aims to boost agricultural productivity and rural economic growth. The scheme has already disbursed over ₹4.47 lakh crore since its launch.

items.title: A deep dive with Rs 84,084 crore scheme for offshore oil and gas exploration
items.summary: The Cabinet approved an ₹84,084-crore scheme for offshore oil and gas exploration. This National Offshore Exploration Scheme, Samudra Manthan, will run until 2030-31. It aims to boost domestic oil and gas production and reserve accretion. The government will fund half the cost of deepwater exploratory drilling. This initiative seeks to de-risk exploration for companies and increase production.
